note: Ratchet for `scripts/loc-metrics.py`. Every number below is lines of git-tracked source, classified by the lexer in `scripts/lib/loc_classify.py`. They may only go DOWN — raising a limit to make a build green defeats the point of measuring, so a rise fails the gate. When a rise is deliberate, run `scripts/loc-metrics.py --baseline` and commit the new file in the SAME commit that grew the tree. Generated files (`@generated` / `DO NOT EDIT` in the header) are measured but excluded from these limits, because appending a wire kind must never fail a size gate. The `*.comment` numbers are measured and diffed but NOT gated: a gate that makes deleting documentation the cheapest way to go green is pointed at the wrong thing.
measured: 2026-08-06 on the full tree at the Plan 11 integration merge. THIRD correction to what the buckets mean, all three the same bug: (1) .mjs/.js were counted as nothing at all -- 45 files, 7,468 lines, including both frontend test suites and the site's whole generator chain -- so moving TypeScript into a .mjs file read as pure reduction; (2) Rust keeps unit tests inside the file they test, and 11,432 of 32,347 Rust code lines (35.3%) sat in #[cfg(test)] blocks counted as production, which is why tracker/src/service.rs read as a 1,228-line monolith when 811 of those lines are its tests; (3) ts now splits main from test the way java and rust already did. The tree did not change. rust.main 31,448 -> 19,997 and ts 11,405 -> 12,720 main + 3,217 test are re-measurements, not movement.
